verdict.rationale: Delaware publishes exact deadlines and penalties: corporate annual reports and franchise taxes are due by March 1, and late filing incurs a $200 penalty plus 1.5% interest per month on tax and penalty. It also lists the June 1 deadline for the $400 alternative-entity tax and the quarterly estimated-tax installment dates and percentages. missing for 10: a published penalty/interest figure for the June 1 alternative-entity tax and for missed quarterly installments in the evidence, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a founder, the filing deadlines and the penalty and interest schedule for missing them are published with exact figures

citations.quote: All active Domestic Corporation Annual Reports and Franchise Taxes for the prior year are due annually on or before March 1st and are required to be filed online. Failure to file the report and pay the required franchise taxes will result in a penalty of $200.00 plus 1.5% interest per month on tax and penalty.
they are required to pay an annual tax of $400.00. Taxes for these entities are due on or before June 1st of each year
Taxpayers owing $5,000.00 or more pay estimated taxes in quarterly installments with 40% due June 1, 20% due by September 1, 20% due by December 1, and the remainder due March 1.
